title: Brittle Split Parsing (BRITTLE_SPLIT_PARSING)
pattern: Extracting structured fields from serialized strings by repeatedly calling unescaped split functions or raw character scan loops without structural grammar or tokenization state.
why_bad: It breaks immediately on escaped delimiters (e.g., CSV fields containing nested commas like `"Smith, John"`), leading to field misalignment, unvalidated/missing data, and silent downstream state corruption. It lacks grammar validation and error recovery.
detection: Look for calls to string split methods (like `.split()`, `.split_whitespace()`, or primitive character-loop delimiter checks) where the resulting segments are immediately mapped to fields of a record or struct, without escaping/quoting checks.
fix: Replace ad-hoc splits with a standards-compliant lexer/parser or a parser combinator library that handles quoting, nesting, and escaped character semantics correctly.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete, 2nd Edition (2004)*, Page 724; *Andrew Hunt & David Thomas - The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Edition (2019)*, Chapter 5.
